facts.statement: The fossil of Iberomesornis was discovered in 1985 by Armando Díaz Romeral at Las Hoyas in east central Spain.
facts.quote: In 1985 the fossil of Iberomesornis was discovered by Armando Díaz Romeral in the Early Cretaceous Calizas de La Huérguina Formation at Las Hoyas, Cuenca Province, east central Spain

facts.statement: The species Iberomesornis romerali was named and described in 1992 by José Luis Sanz and José Fernando Bonaparte.
facts.quote: In 1992 the type species Iberomesornis romerali was named and described by José Luis Sanz and José Fernando Bonaparte

facts.statement: Iberomesornis had a wingspan of about twenty centimetres and a weight estimated at fifteen to twenty grammes.
facts.quote: On the assumption it had relatively short wings, the wingspan was about twenty centimetres; its weight has been estimated at fifteen to twenty grammes

facts.statement: Iberomesornis bore a single claw on each wing.
facts.quote: It bore a single claw on each wing

facts.statement: The preserved axial column length of Iberomesornis is eighty-seven millimetres.
facts.quote: The preserved axial column length is eighty-seven millimetres

facts.statement: The ribcage of Iberomesornis was not strengthened by ossified uncinate processes, though cartilaginous processes were likely present.
facts.quote: Its ribcage was not strengthened by ossified uncinate processes but cartilaginous processes were likely present

facts.statement: The shorter tail and higher shoulder position of Iberomesornis improved manoeuvrability, turning, and swooping at speed.
facts.quote: The shorter tail and the higher position of the shoulder indicated by the strut-like coracoid — allowing for a greater wing amplitude — improved manoeuvrability, turning and swooping at speed

facts.statement: Iberomesornis was a sparrow-sized bird and a constant flyer.
facts.quote: Iberomesornis era un ave del tamaño de un gorrión y un constante volador

facts.statement: The feet of Iberomesornis had three toes pointing forward and one backward, making it one of the first arboreal birds.
facts.quote: Las patas de Iberomesornis presentaban esta misma constitución: tres de los dedos se dirige hacia adelante y uno hacia atrás; es una de las primeras aves arborícolas

facts.statement: Iberomesornis lived on the margins of a large shallow lake where crocodiles, turtles, and a variety of fish were abundant.
facts.quote: Iberomesornis vivió en los márgenes de un gran lago poco profundo donde abundaban los cocodrilos, tortugas y una gran variedad de peces

facts.statement: Iberomesornis was described as a small bird about twenty centimetres long.
facts.quote: Iberomesornis fue descrito como una pequeña ave de unos 20 centímetros de largo

facts.statement: The diet of Iberomesornis consisted of small insects and crustaceans.
facts.quote: Su dieta la constituían insectos y crustáceos pequeños

facts.statement: Today, Iberomesornis is classified within Ornithothoraces as a basal member of the Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: Today, Iberomesornis is seen as positioned within Ornithothoraces, as a basal member of the Enantiornithes

facts.statement: Iberomesornis belongs to the family Iberomesornithidae.
Iberomesornis romerali presents derived physical characteristics compared to Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Iberomesornis romerali presenta característica físicas derivadas respecto a Archaeopteryx

facts.statement: Due to the lack of a skull, it is impossible to know for certain its diet, although no purely herbivorous bird has been found so far.
facts.quote: Debido a la falta del cráneo es imposible saber a ciencia cierta su alimentación, aunque hasta ahora no ha existido un ave netamente herbívora

facts.statement: The time range for Iberomesornis is the Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)
